calls.head: Strength vs. strength
calls.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Connelly has two goals and an assist as the Golden Knights beat the Oilers
paras: Jack Eichel struck first for the Golden Knights on the power play early in the first, with Mitch Marner picking up his 600th NHL assist on the goal. Trevor Connelly made it 2-0 just under three minutes later, but Colton Dach got the Oilers on the board early in the second. Connor McDavid tied it up with 19 seconds left in the period. The third period was a wild one. Nic Dowd and Eichel scored less than four minutes apart early in the period to put the Knights up 4-2. Vasily Podkolzin pulled the Oilers within one just 16 seconds later, and Connelly struck again into the empty net with two and a half minutes left. Connelly added an assist for a three-point night.

The Golden Knights had a bit more of the good stuff. Carter Hart made 21 saves for the Golden Knights, and Devon Levi stopped 22 of 26 at the other end. The Golden Knights improved to 15-6-5, second in the Pacific, while the Oilers dropped to 17-6-4, still first in the Pacific.
